text: ## Introduction Input validation is performed to ensure only properly formed data enters the workflow of an information system, preventing malformed data from persisting in the database and triggering malfunction of various downstream components. Input validation must be applied at every tier of the application (client, server, and database layer). Server-side validation is mandatory — client-side validation is convenience only and can be trivially bypassed.

text: ## Data Type and Length Validation Always validate data type and length before processing: - Strings: maximum length enforced; reject binary or non-printable characters where not expected. - Integers/Floats: parse strictly, enforce min/max range. - Email addresses: validate against RFC 5321 structure; never use regex alone as sole sanitization. - File uploads: validate MIME type server-side (not client-supplied Content-Type), check magic bytes, enforce maximum file size.

text: ## Encoding and Escaping Validation does not replace proper output encoding.
